source_refs.title: Eureka Math / EngageNY, Grade 1, Module 4, Lesson 1

subject: math

objective.text: Count groups of ten faster than counting ones. Show tens and ones in a number bond.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: compare the efficiency of counting by ones and counting by tens

explanations.title: Count tens, not ones
explanations.text: Counting 40 cubes by ones takes a long time. Make 4 ten-sticks and count by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. You get the same number, but it is faster.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: make 4 ten-sticks; counting by tens is more efficient

explanations.title: A number bond for tens and ones
explanations.text: 12 cubes are 1 ten-stick and 2 extra ones. A number bond shows the grouped tens and the extra ones. 12 is made of 10 and 2.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 12 is made of 10 and 2 extra ones

explanations.title: Count the tens first
explanations.text: Count the tens first, then the ones. For 35, say 10, 20, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35. Or say 10, 20, 30, and 5 is 35.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: for 35, one student may count 10, 20, 30, 31 ... 35

examples.title: 12 cubes

examples.title: 35 cubes
